blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Before he was king, David was out in the wilderness with about six hundred men. They camped near the flocks of a rich man named Nabal, and they kept his shepherds safe day and night. At sheep-shearing time, David sent ten young men to ask Nabal kindly for whatever he could spare.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Nabal sent them back with insults. Who is David? When David heard that, he told four hundred men to strap on their swords.

verses.text: But one of the young men told Abigail, Nabal’s wife, saying, Behold, David sent messengers out of the wilderness to salute our master; and he railed on them.

verses.text: But the men were very good unto us, and we were not hurt, neither missed we any thing, as long as we were conversant with them, when we were in the fields:

blocks.text: Notice that servant did not go to Nabal. He went to Abigail. He knew who would listen, and he knew who had sense.

verses.text: Then Abigail made haste, and took two hundred loaves, and two bottles of wine, and five sheep ready dressed, and five measures of parched corn, and an hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and laid them on asses.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: David was hot. His anger was carrying him toward something he could never take back. He meant to wipe out every man in that house by morning.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Nabal means fool, and Abigail did not pretend otherwise. She took the blame on herself and asked David to hear her out.

verses.text: Now therefore, my lord, as the LORD liveth, and as thy soul liveth, seeing the LORD hath withholden thee from coming to shed blood, and from avenging thyself with thine own hand, now let thine enemies, and they that seek evil to my lord, be as Nabal.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: She reminded David who he was. He fought the LORD's battles. He did not need to fight this one. One day he would sit on the throne, and she did not want him to get there with innocent blood on his hands.

verses.text: And David said to Abigail, Blessed be the LORD God of Israel, which sent thee this day to meet me:

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: David did not just say she was right. He said, blessed be the LORD who sent you. He saw God's hand in that woman standing in the road.

verses.text: So David received of her hand that which she had brought him, and said unto her, Go up in peace to thine house; see, I have hearkened to thy voice, and have accepted thy person.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: One woman, some donkeys loaded with bread, and a few wise words turned four hundred swords around. Abigail had no army. She had wisdom and courage and good timing. Thank God for the women who step into the road and keep somebody from a mistake they cannot undo.
